items.name: Blemish / Scar
items.looks: Superficial tan or brown scars, corky or rough patches on the surface.
items.cause: Mechanical injury or rubbing against stems or branches during growth.
items.prevention: Handle fruits carefully and provide plant support to minimize friction.

items.name: Worm Bite / Insect Hole
items.looks: Visible small holes, tunnels, or eaten areas on the tomato surface.
items.cause: Insect pests like fruitworms and caterpillars feeding on the fruit.
items.prevention: Use insect nets, natural repellents, or biological pest control methods.

items.name: Sunscald
items.looks: White or pale patches on sun-exposed areas that later turn papery or sunken.
items.cause: Overexposure to direct sunlight especially after leaf loss.
items.prevention: Maintain good leaf cover; avoid heavy pruning and sudden exposure.

items.name: Cracks / Split
items.looks: Circular or radial cracks around the stem end of the fruit.
items.cause: Irregular watering or sudden rain after dry periods.
items.prevention: Water regularly and avoid extreme soil moisture changes.

items.name: Blemish / Scratch
items.looks: Shallow scars or surface abrasions on the fruit skin.
items.cause: Contact with branches, rough handling, or pest feeding.
items.prevention: Handle fruits gently and minimize plant contact with sharp objects.

items.name: Worm Bite / Chewed Area
items.looks: Holes or irregularly chewed portions on fruit walls.
items.cause: Chewing insects or caterpillars feeding on developing fruit.
items.prevention: Apply organic insect barriers and remove affected fruits early.

items.name: Shrivel / Dehydration
items.looks: Wrinkled or shriveled fruit surface, dull color, and reduced firmness.
items.cause: Loss of moisture during storage or exposure to high temperature.
items.prevention: Store in cool, humid conditions and harvest before over-ripening.

items.name: Uneven Color
items.looks: Patchy color or inconsistent ripening on the fruit surface.
items.cause: Nutrient imbalance or inadequate sunlight exposure.
items.prevention: Ensure balanced fertilization and uniform sunlight distribution.

items.name: Cold Injury (Chilling)
items.looks: Watery, soft, or darkened areas after exposure to cold storage.
items.cause: Exposure to temperatures below 7°C (45°F) during storage or transport.
items.prevention: Store peppers at safe temperature ranges (7–10°C).
